next_row.boundary_rationale: This admonition opens on a universal maxim, “כִּ֣י אָדָ֔ם אֵ֥ין צַדִּ֖יק בָּאָ֑רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַעֲשֶׂה טּ֖וֹב וְלֹ֥א יֶחֱטָֽא” (oshb:Eccl.7.20, byte tier), “Surely there is not a righteous man on earth who does good and doesn't sin” (web:Eccl.7.20). This span's own opening כי is asseverative (WEB “Surely”), distinct from the causal כי that opens oshb:Eccl.7.12 (WEB “For,” “כִּ֛י בְּצֵ֥ל הַֽחָכְמָ֖ה”); the same particle carries different discourse functions at the two sites. The verse's own “צַדִּ֖יק” echoes the paradox-noun already carried forward from oshb:Eccl.7.15 into oshb:Eccl.7.16, disclosed here as texture. The next verse applies the maxim as a practical corollary introduced by “גַּ֤ם” (oshb:Eccl.7.21, byte tier), “גַּ֤ם לְכָל הַדְּבָרִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יְדַבֵּ֔רוּ אַל תִּתֵּ֖ן לִבֶּ֑ךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא תִשְׁמַ֥ע אֶֽת עַבְדְּךָ֖ מְקַלְלֶֽךָ” (oshb:Eccl.7.21, byte tier), “Also don't take heed to all words that are spoken, lest you hear your servant curse you” (web:Eccl.7.21). The corollary is grounded in the same universal claim, “אֲשֶׁ֥ר גַּם את אַתָּ֖ה קִלַּ֥לְתָּ אֲחֵרִֽים” (oshb:Eccl.7.22, byte tier; the pronoun carries an inline unpointed ketiv immediately corrected by its pointed qere, single-witness WLC), “you yourself have likewise cursed others” (web:Eccl.7.22) -- if no one is without sin, the hearer is no exception. The span is held apart from the wisdom-value maxim before it (no shared vocabulary) and from the wisdom-quest narrative after it (a shift to first-person searching).

The span closes on “that God made mankind upright; but they search for many inventions” (web:Eccl.7.29), a general verdict rather than a continuation of the woman crux, but the same find-root chain (oshb:Eccl.7.27-Eccl.7.29) runs straight through to this closing verse.
